cc:Work.dc:title: Box - House
cc:Work.dc:description:
House shaped box with a 90° gable roof, open at the front
Looking at the open front the box looks like this:
``` /\ / \ | | +----+ ```
Parts: house shaped back plate, two side walls, a floor and two roof panels (45° slope each, 90° at the ridge). The sizes are inner sizes of the rectangular base (x = width, y = depth) and the height h of the walls up to the eaves.
The 45° corner between side wall and roof can't be done with a finger joint. There are two options for the side walls:
* **full**: The walls reach up to the roof and overlap with it. An etched line is added on the outside of each wall: one material thickness below the top edge and shorter than the depth by *cutline_inset*. Remove the material between this line and the top edge of the inside (bevel at 45°) so the roof sits flush on the wall. * **flush**: The walls end flush with the underside of the roof at the outer edge. The back plate sticks out above the wall to cover the small triangular gap between wall and roof.
The two roof panels are joined at the ridge with a finger joint.
Without overhang (*overhang* = 0) the walls are always full height and the back plate is a plain house outline. The roof ends at the inner top corner of the wall.
* **full**: a mitre joint. The wall and the roof meet at an outer angle of 135°, so both parts get a 22.5° bevel. Both are cut a bit longer (by thickness * tan(22.5°)) and get an etched line on the inside (walls) / underside (roof) marking the bevel. Remove the material between the line and the outer edge by filing or sanding at 22.5°. The etched side of all parts is meant to face the inside of the house. * **flush**: the roof ends square at the inner top corner of the wall. No bevel, so a small gap remains on the outside.
The roof depth can be set independently with *roof_depth* (0 = same as y), e.g. to let the roof overlap to the front.
The second wall is mirrored so the etched line is on the outside of both walls when the parts are laid out with the etched side up.
Created with Boxes.py (https://boxes.hackerspace-bamberg.de/) Command line: boxes House Command line short: boxes House
